delete.description: Two steps, like deleting a vehicle. On a live token this REVOKES it: the key stops working immediately, and the row stays so the list can still say what it was called and when it was last used — which is how you find out whether anything was still calling with it. Called again on a token that is already revoked, it DELETES the row. The answer says which step ran. A key owned by the shared auth service can be deleted from this list, but revoking it there is what stops it working.

post.description: Verifies the current password, then sets a new one. Rows that agree are summarised in the counts and omitted from the list. Read-only: nothing is written anywhere. get.description: Periods, not just the current fitting: for each account, every stretch during which a device sat on a vehicle, as FMS recorded it and as master data recorded it. post.description: Marks the schedule in_service, the vehicle under repair, and returns the route from the vehicle's current position to the hangar, with its toll. `toll_rp` is for this vehicle's own class, derived from its axle count; when no axle count is recorded — 47% of the legacy fleet — `toll_by_golongan` lists every class instead and `toll_note` says why. An absent toll always carries a note, because a missing figure would otherwise read as a toll-free trip. Both routing and toll are computed in-house: Valhalla for the route, and FMS's own toll_gates/toll_tariffs for the price, by finding which gates the route passes and which charges they make up. A gate no tariff covers is priced at zero and NAMED in `toll_unpriced_gates`, so the total is useful while staying visibly short — `toll_note` then reads "at least this much". That distinction matters: Rp 0 for an unpriced gate and Rp 0 for a genuinely toll-free road are the same number meaning opposite things. An external provider remains wired as a fallback for routes the tables cannot price at all.
post.summary: Send a vehicle to a hangar for a due service

get.description: Routes from the vehicle's CURRENT position to the hangar its service schedule names, with the toll for the remaining journey. Read-only and safe to poll: unlike the dispatch call it records nothing, which is what lets Live View draw the remaining path as the truck moves. The figures stored at dispatch are deliberately not reused — the vehicle has been driving since, so they describe a journey that no longer starts where it starts now. `already_there` means the vehicle is inside the hangar's radius and no line is returned.
get.summary: The remaining journey from a vehicle to its hangar

get.description:
Every non-archived truck of the caller's account with its tracker's last location, its assigned driver's last K-Trip phone location, and the straight-line distance between them in metres. The response shape matches the old GPS platform's feed field for field, so an existing consumer can switch without changing its parser.

Rules carried over from that feed: `_id` and `driver` are master-data ObjectIds; `lastLocation` falls back to the driver's phone fix when it is newer than the tracker's last fix (distance is then 0, and `lastGPS` still shows the tracker's own last fix time); tracker `batteryLevel` is the external supply in volts, flagged in `errorDesc` as BATT_LOW under 8 V and BATT_WARNING under 24.5 V; LOST_GPS is added for a 0,0 fix. Positions are null when telemetry has none (or is unreachable).

Authenticate with the account's API key (`Authorization: Bearer fms_...` or `X-Api-Key: fms_...`) or a signed-in session.

post.description: The figures from the history panel — distance, max speed, harsh events, idle — for a list of trucks named by plate or id, in ONE request. Plates are matched loosely, so "B 9012 UBC", "B9012UBC" and "b-9012-ubc" are one truck. Give neither list to get every tracked vehicle in the account. No track points come back; `fields` chooses which figures to compute, defaulting to the panel's own set. Up to 50 vehicles and 31 days per call. A vehicle whose telemetry cannot be read comes back as a row carrying `error`, so one dead tracker does not fail the batch. READ `distance_source` AND `events_sampled` ON EACH ROW: distance is measured from every sample when the window starts at a local midnight and ends at a day boundary or now, and walked along a downsampled track otherwise; the event counts are lower bounds whenever the samples behind them are more than 30s apart.

delete.description: Two steps, because "delete" means two things. On an active vehicle this archives it: out of live view and the registry's default list, still there to explain past trips, and retired in master data so the projection does not restore it. Called again on a vehicle that is ALREADY archived, it deletes the row for good, together with the FMS records that name it (alerts, service schedules, score events, SOP runs, documents) and, by cascade, its telemetry state, geofence membership, rule attachments and tracker fit history. Telemetry itself — positions and trips — lives in the other database keyed by IMEI and is not touched. The response says which step ran.

get.description: Map-matches the raw GPS trace so the line follows roads instead of cutting corners and wandering through buildings. Where the matcher cannot join two consecutive fixes it ends one match and begins another, leaving a short hole — usually a couple of kilometres at an interchange; those holes are closed by routing between the two matched ends, and `gaps_bridged` counts them, because a bridged stretch is inferred rather than observed. `chunks_matched` below `chunks_total` means a whole section failed, typically an unmapped yard or plantation track. Costs several provider requests (the trace is split into chunks of 200 fixes and matched in parallel), so it is requested explicitly rather than being folded into the history response — and the raw trace remains available, because the matched line is an interpretation and the fixes themselves are what matter in a dispute. `distance_km` is measured along roads. `chunks_matched` below `chunks_total` means part of the journey was unmatchable — typically an unmapped yard or plantation track.
get.summary: A vehicle's travelled path, snapped to the road network
Rules applicable to a vehicle, each flagged attached/not

post.summary: Attach a rule to a vehicle

delete.summary: Detach a rule from a vehicle

get.summary: Accumulated telemetry state for a vehicle (engine hours, odometer, battery)

get.description: Newest first. Deleted auto-saved clips are hidden unless status=deleted. Without a status filter, an event's "no clip" or failed row is also hidden once that event has a saved or downloading video (any camera for "no clip", the same camera for failed). from/to are WIB days (YYYY-MM-DD) on the clip time. Without limit it returns up to 500, as before.
get.summary: Saved clips (accident evidence)

get.description: Totals, per WIB day, per event type and per truck for automatically saved clips. Each event + camera counts once by its latest row; deleted clips are left out; still-downloading clips are left out of the sizes. events_with_video / events_camera_didnt_send / events_save_failed put each event in one outcome, however many cameras it has. Same access as the clip list.
get.summary: Saved Evidence summary (automatic saves)

get.description: The same numbers as /v1/video-clips/summary for the same window and customer, as a PDF: overview, per event type, per truck, and what every term means. English, no AI text.
get.summary: Saved Evidence summary as a PDF

delete.description: Removes the S3 object, and the video_clips record (an auto-saved clip keeps it as 'deleted' so it isn't saved again). 409 while the clip is still downloading. Manager+.

get.description:
Presigned S3 GET URL. ?download=1 forces a file download; else it
plays inline in the browser.
get.summary: A short-lived URL to view or download a saved clip
Configured alarm webhooks

post.summary: Add an alarm webhook
Send a test event to a webhook

catalog.description: built client-side from the metric registry

locale.description:
Locale is the user's UI language. Asking the model to "reply in the
language of the request" was not enough on its own — an Indonesian
request came back with English titles — so the expected language is
stated outright rather than inferred.

unmapped.description:
Unmapped names spreadsheet headers no report can supply. Surfaced rather
than dropped: a report that quietly omits a column the user asked for is
worse than one that says it cannot fill it.

by_code.description:
ByCode is the fleet-wide tally, for a headline that does not need the
per-vehicle breakdown summed client-side.

scorecard.description: Scorecard indicates this alert type also feeds Driver Scorecard scoring.

checked_by.description: Who last changed check_status (a user id; the client resolves the name).

counts.description:
Counts is keyed by ALERT CODE (OVERSPEED, HARSH_BRAKING, …), not by any
consumer's categories: a caller groups codes into its own kinds, and
this service does not inherit a vocabulary it cannot test.

issued_here.description:
IssuedHere distinguishes a key FMS minted and verifies itself from one
the shared auth service owns. It decides where revoking actually has to
happen, so the list can say so instead of letting someone revoke a copy
and wonder why the key still works.

token.description: Token is populated ONLY in the create response (shown once).

deleted.description: Deleted is the second: the row goes too.

revoked.description:
Revoked is the first step: the key stops working, the row stays so the
list still shows what it was and when it was last used.

from.description: RFC3339, only when Preset is empty

preset.description: Preset is one of the RangePreset values. When set, From/To are ignored.

day_of_week.description: DayOfWeek is 0=Sunday, weekly only. DayOfMonth is 1-28, monthly only.

report_name.description:
ReportName is joined in for display, so a list of schedules is readable
without a second request per row.

columns.description:
Columns optionally narrows and reorders the source's columns, and can
rename them. Empty means "all of them, as the source ordered them".

Renaming matters more than it looks: the point of a custom report is
often that someone downstream expects "Nopol" where we say
"license_plate", and forcing them to rename it every month is exactly
the friction this feature exists to remove.

note.description: Note is printed under the section, for context the numbers do not carry.

format.description: Format is the default the user picked; the download can override it.

narrative.description:
Narrative overrides the by-format default: prose for pdf/docx, raw tables
for xlsx/csv. Nil means "use the default", which is almost always right —
the point is that the same saved report gives an executive a readable
document and an analyst a spreadsheet, without being configured twice.

notes.description: free text printed under the title

is_demo.description:
IsDemo: this account only demos the camera; another account owns it.
Not registered in master data.

alarm_id.description:
AlarmID is the camera event an auto-saved clip belongs to; EventCode and
EventName name it. All nil for manual saves.

job_id.description: JobID of the telemetry download, for polling live stage while pending. Empty on list.

status.description: pending | ready | failed | no_clip | deleted. s3_key/bucket are null until ready.

avg_events_per_truck_day.description: Averages over the trucks with events and every day of the window.

is_demo.description: IsDemo: a copy of another account's camera, shown here for a demo.

alarm_id.description:
AlarmID links an SD-card pull to the camera event it replaces, so the
Saved Evidence summary counts that event as saved. Optional; it must be
an event this camera already has a clip row for.

required_headers.description:
The client MUST send exactly these on the PUT or S3 rejects the
signature. Returned explicitly so the caller does not have to infer them.

dev.description:
Dev marks a roadmap module that isn't built yet: it appears in the
configurator (so an account can pre-enable it) and the sidebar shows it as
a stub, but there's no working page behind it yet.

litres.description: estimated fuel used (nil = no km/L set)

min_dwell_min.description:
MinDwellMin is how long a vehicle must stay inside before it counts as
having arrived. 0 means the first fix inside counts, which is right for
a large site and wrong for a small one on a through road.

present.description: Present is how many vehicles are inside right now.

watching.description: Watching is how many vehicles are attached; 0 means the whole fleet.

booked.description:
Booked counts open service schedules pointing here; Present counts
vehicles physically inside the radius right now. See the package comment:
these are different numbers and the gap between them is the signal.

already_there.description:
AlreadyThere is true when the vehicle is inside the hangar radius, in
which case no route was requested at all.

duration_min.description:
DurationMin is the provider's free-flow estimate. Named plainly rather
than "ETA" because it contains no traffic, no loading time and no driver
break — calling it an ETA would promise something it cannot know.

distance_m.description:
DistanceM is how far away it is, so a no-show can be chased. Only set
for vehicles that have NOT arrived.

present.description:
Present is whether the vehicle is physically here right now, which is not
the same as being booked here.

since.description:
Since and DwellMin are the arrival time and how long it has been here —
the difference between "it is at the workshop" and "it has been at the
workshop for three days".

headline.description:
Headline is a ready-to-display sentence, built server-side so every client
and the AI narrator describe a finding identically.

metric.description: Metric is which measure moved: idle_pct | distance | moving_hours | stopped.

sigma.description:
Sigma is how many standard deviations of this vehicle's OWN daily spread
the change represents. Exposed because it is the number that decides
whether a finding is real, and hiding it would make the ranking look
arbitrary beside the more eye-catching percentage.

kind.description:
Kind separates a real battery problem from an implausible reading:
"battery" | "sensor_fault". They need different people and different
parts, so collapsing them into one list wastes a trip.

scheduled.description:
Scheduled reports whether a battery service is ALREADY booked for this
vehicle, so the client shows "scheduled" rather than offering the action
again — and so a second click cannot create a duplicate.

due_in_days.description: DueInDays is negative when already overdue, null when not time-based.

kind.description: Kind is the source: alert | document | service | idle_asset | battery.

rank.description:
Rank is the computed priority; exposed so the client can show why an item
sits where it does rather than presenting an inscrutable order.

ref_id.description:
RefID identifies the row within its kind, so the client can deep-link and
(for alerts) mark it checked.

due_in_days.description: DueInDays defaults by severity when omitted.

value.description: km/h over limit, or km/h/s for harsh

fuel_ratio_kmpl.description:
Vehicle fuel config, echoed so the client can turn distance into an
estimated litres consumed for this trip. Null when the vehicle has no
figures set — the estimate is then simply not shown.

hull_no.description: HullNo is the truck's hull number (nomor lambung) as set on the vehicle. Null when none is set.

license_plate.description:
The truck's nomor polisi, so a caller that asked by hull number can
tell which truck answered.

distance_source.description:
How much of the track these figures were actually derived from.

The panel offers windows up to "custom", and the track is capped at
5,000 points however long the window is. Over a day that is 17-second
resolution and everything below is exact; over 52 days it is one point
every 15 minutes, and walking THAT recovers about a quarter of the real
distance while counting almost no harsh events — silently, with the
same confident tiles. These fields are what let the answer say so.

DistanceSource is "rollup" when distance and max speed came from the
telemetry service's per-sample daily aggregate instead of the sampled
track, which is the only way those two can be right over a long window.

events_sampled.description:
EventsSampled says the overspeed and harsh counts are a LOWER BOUND:
harsh detection needs consecutive samples within 30s, and at this gap
most pairs were skipped.

idle_by_reason.description:
IdleByReason splits TotalIdleMin by why the truck stood still (see
classifyStop). "loading" and "traffic" are the job; "rest" and "unknown"
are what a fleet manager can actually act on.

sample_gap_s.description:
SampleGapS is the median seconds between the points the event counts
were derived from.

active.description:
Active counts vehicles that reported at all; Unused counts those that
reported but never moved — an idle asset, not an offline one.

idle_pct.description:
IdlePct is idle as a share of engine-on time, over vehicles that ACTUALLY
MOVED that day. Including never-moved vehicles folds stuck-ignition
sensors into the fleet's headline waste number: 13 devices report the
engine on for 24h while covering 0 km, and they are a wiring fault, not
a driver leaving an engine running.

component.description:
Component is what the vehicle was sent in for, so the map can say
"brakes" rather than only naming a destination.

dispatched_at.description:
DispatchedAt, with DistanceKm and EtaMin, are AS MEASURED WHEN SENT and
are not refreshed. The vehicle has been moving since, so treating them
as current would misreport progress; the live position is next to them
in this same record, and a caller wanting the remaining distance should
ask for a fresh route rather than trust these.

master_data_id.description:
MasterDataID is the shared-platform driver id — the identity the K-Trip
phone app reports positions under. Empty when the driver is unpaired.

by_axis.description: always X, Y, Z (zeroed if none)

cost_basis.description:
Cost efficiency. Fuel cost basis is sensor-measured when a fuel sensor +
tank are set (captures idle burn); otherwise the configured km/L rate
(which does NOT see idle, so it under-counts on idle-heavy trips).

engine_hours.description: Operating time over the window, from ignition + speed per fix.

fuel_readings.description: points that carried a fuel level

refuels.description: where + how much + cost, per refuel

thefts.description:
Suspected fuel thefts (large fast drops). Always surfaced on the history —
no toggle — because a theft is not something to opt into seeing.

reason.description:
Reason: loading | traffic | rest | unknown — why the truck stood still,
so idle time is not judged subjectively (feedback epic 2.2). Place names
the geofence for a loading stop.

address.description:
Address is the most specific place name available, ready to display —
street when there is one, otherwise district and city.

A third of the fleet's fixes carry no street: yards, ports and
plantation roads have no name, and Semarang alone accounts for 250 of
them at any moment. A consumer that shows `jalan` and falls back to
"unknown" therefore labels ~600 trucks unknown while knowing their
district and city perfectly well — which is what TMS's Control Tower
did. Composing it here means every consumer gets the same answer and
none has to know the five fields' precedence.

metadata.description:
Metadata is the raw per-device sensor blob (fuel, voltages, GSM/GNSS, etc.).
Only populated on the single-vehicle detail path; the bulk list trims it.

source.description:
Source is where the fix came from, in order of preference: "tracker"
(GPS unit), "camera" (the dashcam's own GPS, for vehicles without a
tracker), or "phone" (the assigned driver's K-Trip app, when neither
device has a fix). A phone follows the person, not the truck: it
locates the vehicle only while that driver is assigned to it.

chunks_total.description:
ChunksMatched below ChunksTotal means part of the journey could not be
matched — typically an unmapped yard or plantation track. Surfaced so the
UI can say the line is incomplete rather than presenting a gap as fact.

distance_km.description:
DistanceKm is measured along roads. Verified against a day whose distance
was known independently from the daily rollup: 489 km matched vs 461.5 km
recorded, i.e. ~6% over, which is what following real road geometry
instead of straight lines between fixes should produce.

gaps_bridged.description:
GapsBridged counts holes in the match that were closed by routing between
two matched segments.

The matcher restarts wherever it cannot join two consecutive fixes,
leaving a short hole — usually a couple of kilometres around an
interchange. Both ends are already snapped to the road network, so
routing across is reliable, but it is an inference about a stretch that
was never observed. Surfaced so the caption can say so.

partial.description:
Partial is set when the matched path is implausibly short against
StraightLineKm. Roads cannot be shorter than the straight lines between
their own points, so a matched distance well below it is arithmetically
impossible for a complete path — which makes this detectable rather than
something a reader has to notice.

When true the line is a fragment: show it as incomplete, and do not use
DistanceKm as a distance.

straight_line_km.description:
StraightLineKm is the great-circle distance through the raw fixes: the
shortest the journey could possibly have been.

It exists because ChunksMatched == ChunksTotal does NOT mean the whole
path was found. A chunk can come back SHORT and still report complete
success: no error, one plausible line, a distance that is simply too
small. This number is the floor that makes that detectable.

It earned its place by catching a real one. trace_route reports a
discontinuous match as several trips, and this client read only the
first — so a 99 km stretch that matched as 37,7 + 10,3 + 46,5 km was
reported as 37,7 km with every appearance of success. Figures once
quoted here about matching degrading with fix spacing came from the same
blind spot and should not be reused.

fields.description:
Fields chooses what to compute and return. Empty means the default set
(everything in the history panel). Unknown names are rejected rather
than ignored, because a typo that silently drops a column is found in
production by the person reading the spreadsheet.

from.description:
From and To are RFC3339. A window longer than 31 days is refused: the
figures are computed from the raw track, and a year of forty trucks is
not a request, it is an outage.

idle_threshold_min.description: IdleThresholdMin is how long a stop must last to count as idle; default 5.

overspeed_limit.description: OverspeedLimit (km/h) decides what counts as overspeed; default 60.

plates.description:
Plates and VehicleIDs both select vehicles; give either or both. Empty
means every vehicle in the account that has a tracker — convenient, and
slow enough on a large fleet that it is not the default anyone reaches
for by accident.

not_found.description:
NotFound lists plates that matched no vehicle, so a caller can tell a
typo from a quiet truck.

distance_source.description:
How far to trust the figures above, per vehicle — because it varies per
vehicle: two trucks over the same window can have very different
reporting density, and one of them can be well sampled while the other
is not.

DistanceSource is "rollup" when distance and max speed were measured
from every sample, "track" when they were walked along a downsampled
path and are therefore UNDERSTATED.

error.description:
Error is set when this vehicle's figures could not be computed — the
rest of the fleet still comes back, with this row saying why it did not.

events_sampled.description:
EventsSampled marks overspeed_count, harsh_accel and harsh_brake as
LOWER BOUNDS. Harsh detection compares consecutive fixes less than 30s
apart; over a long window most pairs are further apart than that, so
most of the period was never examined. A caller that sums these across
a fleet without checking this flag is adding up floors.

sample_gap_s.description: SampleGapS is the median seconds between the samples behind the counts.

idle_min.description: IdleMin is how long the vehicle sat at this point's stop (0 while moving).

over_limit.description: OverLimit is true when Speed exceeds the requested limit at this point.

source.description:
Source is "tracker" or "camera". Always set; matters when a caller asks
for both and gets one interleaved track to draw as two.

fuel.description: distance, litres, cost, km/L, Rp/km, Rp/hour, refuels, engine/idle/moving hours

state.description: lifetime engine hours, odometer, service context

battery_v.description:
From the telemetry collector's state table (updated ~2min) — cheap to
join fleet-wide, powers list filters without shipping metadata blobs.

camera_device_id.description:
CameraDeviceID is the linked dashcam's VSS id, when the vehicle has one.
Present whether or not the camera is the position source.

dispatch.description:
Dispatch is set while the vehicle is on its way to a hangar for service.

Live View's job is to answer "where is this truck and what is it doing".
A truck taken off the road and sent for repair is doing something, and
without this the map showed it driving with no indication of why or
where to — the dispatch was recorded in Maintenance and invisible here,
which is the one screen an operator actually watches.

km_since_service.description:
Maintenance context: km driven since the last recorded service. Nil when
unknown; HasServiceRecord=false means no maintenance record exists yet.

master_data_id.description:
MasterDataID is the vehicle's id in karlo_masterdata — the identity the
rest of the platform keys on. VehicleID above is FMS-local and means
nothing to TMS, so a caller correlating a truck across products joins on
this. NULL until vehiclesync has paired the row; the alternative for
callers is matching on the plate, which is not a stable identity (see
migration 0042 — this dataset contains six re-plated trucks).

state_since.description:
StateSince is when the current DriveState began, so a list can say
"idle for 40 min" instead of a speed. Moving/idle/parking come from the
telemetry current-state row, which keeps the timestamp of the last
class change; for offline it is the last fix (the truck has not been
heard from since). Omitted for camera-only positions and for rows
written before the telemetry service kept it.

tank_litres.description:
TankLitres is the vehicle's fuel tank size, from the FMS vehicle
record (master data does not carry it). Nil when nobody has set it.

tenant_id.description:
Owning account — populated ONLY in the platform-admin cross-tenant list, so
the operator (and the detail panel) knows which account a vehicle is in.

done_at.description:
DoneAt defaults to today. Supplied when the paperwork lands later than
the work did, which is the normal case.

next_due_at.description:
NextDueAt and NextOdometer are computed by the caller from the
schedule's own interval. Left here rather than derived in SQL so the
arithmetic lives in one language, beside the rules that set it at
creation.

odometer.description:
Odometer at completion. Rolls the next interval forward from the real
reading rather than from an estimate.

hangar_id.description:
HangarID books the work into a maintenance hangar. Optional: plenty of
service happens roadside or at a third party, and forcing a hangar would
make the field a lie rather than a fact. Setting it is what puts the
vehicle on that hangar's list and makes it routable there.

last_done_at.description:
When the last service happened and the odometer reading at that time —
this is what "km since last service" everywhere is computed from.

hangar_id.description:
HangarID is required here even though the column is nullable, because a
dispatch with no destination is not a dispatch. A schedule can still be
created, and serviced roadside, without one.

already_there.description:
AlreadyThere when the truck is inside the hangar's radius. The schedule
is still dispatched — the work is booked either way — but no route is
returned, because routing a vehicle to where it is standing draws a dot.

geometry.description: Geometry is [lon, lat], ready for a map as a GeoJSON LineString.

toll_golongan.description:
TollGolongan is the class TollRp was taken from, so a disputed figure
can be traced to an assumption rather than argued about blind.

toll_note.description:
TollNote explains an absent figure: no axles recorded, no toll on the
route, or pricing unavailable. An empty toll with no note would read as
"this trip is toll-free".

toll_rp.description:
TollRp is what the trip to the workshop costs in tolls, for THIS
vehicle's class. Nil when the class is unknown or no toll applies —
never zero, because zero asserts the roads are free and a missing axle
count is not that claim.

toll_unpriced_gates.description:
TollUnpricedGates names gates no tariff covered. When present, every
toll figure above is an UNDERSTATEMENT: those gates contributed nothing.
Shown so a cheap route cannot be confused with an unmeasured one — and
each name is a tariff someone can look up.

vehicle_marked_repair.description:
VehicleMarkedRepair is false when the vehicle was archived, since a
retired truck must not be quietly returned to the fleet's active list by
booking a service against it.

already_there.description:
AlreadyThere when the vehicle is inside the hangar's radius. No route is
returned, because routing a vehicle to where it is standing draws a dot.

geometry.description: Geometry is [lon, lat], ready for a map as a GeoJSON LineString.

toll_rp.description:
Toll for the REMAINING journey, recomputed with the route. Same shape
and the same rules as the dispatch response: a single figure when the
vehicle's class is known, every class when it is not, and a note rather
than a zero whenever there is no figure.

vehicle_lat.description:
VehicleLat/Lon are where the route starts: the vehicle's live position,
not where it stood when dispatched.

window_minutes.description:
WindowMinutes, when set, makes this a FREQUENCY rule: fire when >= Threshold
events of AlertCode occur for a vehicle within this many minutes (e.g.
"smoking >= 10 times in 60 minutes"). Nil = an instantaneous rule.

vehicles.description: paired vehicles with at least one resolvable value

match.description:
Match: "brand" | "truck_body" | "truck_head" with the catalogue entry it
resolved to, or "none".

vehicles.description: rows carrying it (paired with master data)

vehicles_unpaired.description:
VehiclesUnpaired: grouped here but with no master_data_id — nothing to
set upstream until vehiclesync pairs them.

vehicle.description: plate where resolvable, else the master-data id

checked.description: Checked is how many devices were compared.

fms_vehicle.description: What each side says, as a plate where FMS can resolve one.

verdict.description:
Verdict:
  agree          — both say the same vehicle (or both say unfitted)
  differ         — fitted to DIFFERENT vehicles. The dangerous one.
  fms_only       — FMS has it on a truck, master data has it in stock
  masterdata_only— master data has it on a truck, FMS has it unfitted
  unpaired       — FMS has no master_data_id for the device yet
  unknown_vehicle— master data names a vehicle FMS cannot resolve

company_id.description: CompanyID is the master-data company (UUID), when the directory knows it.

device_id.description: DeviceID is the IMEI for a GPS unit, the VSS device id for a dashcam.

has_assignment_history.description:
HasAssignmentHistory: fitted_at came from a real tracker_assignments
row. False means the device was imported already on the vehicle and
fitted_at is its created_at — "at least since then", not an install date.

is_demo.description:
IsDemo: a copy of a device owned by another account, shown here for a
demo. Master data keeps the real owner; skip this row when reconciling.

vehicle_id.description: Current fitting: nil when the device is in stock.

geofence_ids.description:
GeofenceIDs narrows the geofence movement report. Empty means every
geofence — "what moved through my sites today" is the question people
actually open that report with, and making them pick one site at a time
turns one answer into eight.

vehicle_ids.description:
VehicleIDs runs a per-vehicle report for SEVERAL vehicles and stacks the
results into one table. Fleet operators think in terms of "these six
trucks", not one at a time, and re-running a report six times and pasting
the output together is the manual work this removes.

from_gate.description:
FromGate is empty on a flat-fee charge. An open or integrated system —
JORR, for instance — takes one tap and a fixed amount, so there is no
exit to name. Those are real charges, not truncated records: one
measured journey carried five of them in a row.

meta.description:
Meta carries the numbers behind the penalty — the specific dates an issue
occurred, the idle percentage — so the detail view can show WHEN and WHY,
not just how many. Shape varies by code; the client reads what it knows.

dwell_min.description:
DwellMin is the finished stay's length, or — while the vehicle is still
there — how long it has been there so far. The field a presence panel
shows, computed here so every caller agrees on it.

open.description: Open says whether the vehicle is still inside.

custom_fuel_price.description:
CustomFuelPrice is the company's own price, or nil = follow the
national price. On PUT, send null to follow, a number to fix it.

fuel_price_per_litre.description:
FuelPricePerLitre is the price in force for this company: its own
fixed price when set, otherwise the national price for FuelType.

fuel_price_source.description: FuelPriceSource explains where FuelPricePerLitre came from.

_id.description:
ID is the truck's master-data ObjectId. Null for a vehicle the
master-data projection has not paired yet.

distanceDriverToTruck.description:
DistanceDriverToTruck is the straight-line distance in metres between
lastLocation and driverLastLocation. Null unless both are present.

driver.description:
Driver is the assigned driver's master-data ObjectId. Absent when the
truck has no driver assigned, as in the legacy feed.

lastLocation.description:
LastLocation is the tracker's latest fix — or the assigned driver's
phone fix when that is newer than anything the tracker has sent (the
legacy rule; the distance is then 0). Null when neither has a fix.

batteryLevel.description: tracker: external supply in volts; phone: percent

lastGPS.description:
LastGPS is the tracker's own latest fix time, even when the position
shown is the phone's. Null when the tracker has never reported.

last_service_km.description:
Maintenance context for the odometer: km driven since the most recent
recorded service. Nil when the vehicle has no service records yet.

by_golongan.description:
ByGolongan is ALL FIVE classes, always, even when axles were supplied.

A caller with an axle count reads its own; one without shows the range
and says which it is. Collapsing to a single figure would mean this
endpoint picking a class on the caller's behalf, silently, for the 47%
of trucks that cannot be classified — and a toll figure becomes a
driver's cash advance.

complete.description:
Complete is UnpricedGates being empty, stated positively so a client
cannot read a missing array as "all good" by accident.

golongan.description:
Golongan is the class implied by the axles supplied, 0 when none were.
Amount is that class's figure, nil when the class is unknown — never
zero, which would read as a free journey.

segments.description:
Segments are the individual charges in travel order. A journey is not
one transaction, and a disputed figure is argued about per gate.

unpriced_gates.description:
UnpricedGates names gates no tariff covered.

WHEN THIS IS NON-EMPTY THE TOTALS ARE AN UNDERSTATEMENT: those gates
contributed nothing, so the real cost is higher by whatever they charge.
Carried rather than swallowed because a caller must be able to tell a
cheap route from an unmeasured one, which the figure alone cannot.

axles.description:
Axles narrows the answer to one class, when the caller knows it.

OPTIONAL, and omitting it is a normal case rather than a lapse: 47% of
the legacy fleet has no axle count recorded. The response carries all
five classes either way — see Quote.

geometry.description:
Geometry is the routed line, [lon, lat] in TRAVEL ORDER. GeoJSON order,
matching what every router here returns, so a caller passes a route's
geometry through untouched.

is_demo.description:
IsDemo: this account only demos the device; its real owner is another
account. Not registered in master data.

IsDemo marks a copy of a device that really belongs to another account
(shown here for a demo). Never paired with or written to master data.

owner.description:
Owner is who owns the hardware — "karlo", "customer" or "vendor" — and
OwnerName is that third party when it is not Karlo's own unit. Both are
projected from master data, which is their only writer, so they are
read-only here and nil for a device master data has not labelled.
This is the field that separates our own trackers from a vendor's feed.

vehicle_plate.description:
VehiclePlate is the truck this device is fitted to right now, nil when
it is in stock. The id alone answers "is it linked"; the plate answers
"to what", which is the question actually being asked.

note.description: Note explains what the caller should expect to see next.

unassigned_from_vehicle.description: Unassigned is the vehicle it was taken off on the way out, if any.

address.description:
Address is the reverse-geocoded position, coarsest-last
("Jl. Sudirman, Menteng, Jakarta Pusat, DKI Jakarta"), sent only when the
link enables the "location" field. Behind a toggle like every other
detail here: the map already shows WHERE a truck is, but a street name
spells out the delivery address in a way a pin does not, and a share link
is public to anyone holding the URL.

duration_hours.description: takes precedence over days when set

own.description: Own is true for the company's private entry (as opposed to Karlo's).

axles.description:
Toll class and lorry dimensions.

Axles decides the toll class — 2 is Golongan II, 3 is III, 4 is IV, 5 or
more is V — and nil means UNKNOWN, never a default. A guessed class
misprices every truck that has a real axle count, and does it invisibly
because the figure looks precise.

GolonganOverride exists because two axles is ambiguous: BPJT splits
two-axle vehicles between Golongan I ("pick up / truk kecil") and
Golongan II on size, which an axle count cannot decide.

The dimensions let routing apply the height, width and weight limits it
already reads from OpenStreetMap; without them every route uses
fleet-wide defaults.

master_data_id.description:
MasterDataID pairs the row with karlo_masterdata (the id TMS uses).
Null until vehiclesync or write-through has paired it.

archived.description: Archived is true for the first step, Deleted for the second.

removed.description:
Removed counts the dependent FMS rows a hard delete destroyed, by kind,
so the answer can say what was lost rather than just "ok".
